title: A scan of 5,445 two-block schedules found no sustained growth in models of two adult worm maps
abstract: We tested periodic whole-map switching in positive linear models of two adult C. elegans chemical wiring cores with 157 common cells. Five weight rules and 1,089 exposure pairs per rule gave 5,445 tests. All schedules decayed over repeated periods at gain 0.99. One local search per rule found no growing schedule. The largest scanned count-weighted one-period norm gain was 2.2792, while its period multiplier was 0.92670. Thus temporary response growth remained possible. A separate positive-vector bound guarantees arbitrary switching only below gain 0.946261 for count weights. The gap to gain 1 remains open. Unit row or column totals give arbitrary-switch stability below gain 1 by construction. A synthetic unstable pair, positive-vector spectral brackets and direct time integration checked the calculation. These results distinguish whole-template switching from prior independent cell profile uncertainty. A finite scan does not prove stability for all schedules. Two selected animals, assumed positive count-based coupling, equal time constants and no matched activity limit biological use. Original code, aggregate outcomes, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records and derived wiring matrices are not bundled.

display.caption: Critical gains for periodic whole-map switching and temporary norm growth under fixed count-weighted maps. The scan does not cover all schedules.
